hypothesis: A population prior in dimension-invariant relation coordinates reduces normal-dynamics estimation error from short personal references and improves future disturbance warning.
normal_coordinates: 15 coordinates per target: two own lag values and masks; two signed shrunken network messages and coverages; three signed shrunken environment messages and coverages; intercept
normalization: each held reference block uses means and standard deviations from its remaining reference dates; monitoring uses all first56 dates; predictors clipped8 after this scaling; original event normalization remains unchanged
relation_messages: pairwise reference correlations shrink by (n-3)/(n-3+24); messages divided by max(1,sum absolute edge weights); own node excluded from network; reference edges refitted within each held-block calculation
population_fit: training participants only; held-block normal-target pairs weighted equally per participant, then per node, then per available date; target clipped8 in training-reference units for fitting only; shared ridge point estimate
training_person_crossfit: subtract that participant's normal-target sufficient statistics before calculating its prior; validation/held people use all training people
personal_fit: ridge around population coefficients or zero coefficients on identical15 coordinates; matched reference-block availability; fewer14 targets retain prior
selection: personal ridge selected by equal-person, equal-node held-reference Huber2 loss in validation people; risk C then selected by validation AUROC; no held development outcomes in either selection; reference MSE/MAE also reported without target clipping
risk_coordinates: 296 existing coordinates; original raw H/N and direct context coordinates reused; conditional residual descriptors and residual network are replaced; environment effect is normalized norm of three learned environment-message coefficients
outcome_and_splits: unchanged original56/32/1/7 protocol and five participant folds; no external test evaluation
novelty_scope: hierarchical regression, parameter priors and VAR forecasts are established methods; evaluate their combination with dimension-invariant relation messages and personal sustained-event warning, without claiming the components are new
